solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Craze about weapons, note, in country area

indicators.note: the word for a craze is wrapped about the other pieces, holding them inside it

parts.note: a craze is a fad
weapons are arms
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale (also spelt ti)

explanation.surface: A weapons fad has taken hold somewhere out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmstead is a farm with its buildings, a piece of rural land.

clue.text: Centre of attention for nearly all clubs, American

indicators.note: nearly all of the word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: An American gets the spotlight at almost every club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' trims 'for' to FO.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is the central point that draws attention or interest.

clue.text: Element that's strange about container that reaches India

indicators.note: the strange word goes about the rest, holding it inside

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd
a hod is a builder's container for carrying bricks
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A curious element surrounds a vessel that got as far as India.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM meaning strange is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodium is a chemical element, a rare silvery metal of the platinum group.

clue.text: Place set somehow to welcome 100 for show

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in another, welcoming it
set out somehow means in some new arrangement

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A venue is arranged to receive a hundred guests for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal rearranges PLACE SET into SPETACLE, and 'to welcome' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public display or show.

clue.text: Giving reasons English vote scheme is supported by a politician

indicators.note: in a down entry the earlier pieces sit above and rest on those below

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot
a plan is a scheme
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: An English voting scheme is explained, with backing from a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is supported by' fits a down clue: E, X and PLAN stand on A and TORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something explanatory serves to explain, setting out the reasons for a thing.

clue.text: Dive in promptly at outset and swim

indicators.note: the outset of each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A swimmer is urged to dive straight in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at outset' picks the first letters of Dive In Promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a quick bathe, a brief swim.

clue.text: Exclusive concession protecting firm

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the concession word holds the firm inside it

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business deal grants one firm sole rights while sheltering it from rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a scoop is a story one paper has exclusively, ahead of rivals.

clue.text: Proved to be quiet, personal

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
one's own is one's personal property

explanation.surface: Something has been demonstrated to be private and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown means demonstrated, as in 'shown to be true'.

clue.text: Island's old family not present, last to go

definitions.note: Island's reads as 'island is', the definition followed by the linking verb

parts.note: kin is family

indicators.note: the final letter goes, being dropped

parts.note: away means not present

explanation.surface: An islander's old family has gone, the last of them departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to go' trims AWAY to AWA.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is a Japanese island, the largest of the Ryukyu chain.

clue.text: Host kind of tense, I hesitate to say

parts.note: the present is a grammatical tense
er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A host is in a tense state and hesitant to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter hosts a television or radio programme.

clue.text: Maybe still go down in competition

indicators.note: the word for going down sits in the word for a competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition
to go down in a contest is to lose

explanation.surface: Someone may yet be knocked out of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe still' looks like 'perhaps yet'; it is the definition, a still being a single photograph or film frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a kind of shot, and a still photograph may be one, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Writing about Mediterranean's No. 1 island shows potential

indicators.note: the writing word is placed about the next two pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing

indicators.note: the number one letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: A text about a leading Mediterranean island reveals what it could become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M and I inside PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Promise is the noun for signs of future excellence, i.e. potential.

clue.text: Paul, say, succeeded with excellent later books

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as the letter I
NT, the New Testament, contains the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: The apostle Paul thrived, his excellent letters forming the Bible's later books.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul the apostle is an example of a saint; 'say' marks him as one instance.

clue.text: Adjunct program finish is ahead of time

indicators.note: the program and finish words come in front of the time word

parts.note: an app is a computer program
an end is a finish
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A supplementary piece of software finishes before its deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added on to a larger thing, an adjunct.

clue.text: A favourite singer or one up to no good?

parts.note: a means per, as in 'twice a day'
a pet is a favourite
a rat sings to the police: informers are said to sing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the much-loved crooner a villain?
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is underworld slang: an informer sings, and a rat is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A perpetrator carries out a wrongful act, a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Parent, silent

definitions.meaning: the British everyday word for mother
to keep ... is to stay silent

explanation.definitionFit: Mum is a mother, and as an adjective it means saying nothing.

clue.text: Tours arranged after battle? Shocking

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the battle word

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a First World War battle

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Tours of a battlefield have been organised, appallingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges TOURS into TROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstrous means outrageous or appalling, as shocking things are.

clue.text: Unfortunate actor vainly claiming to know what happens next?

definitions.text: claiming to know what happens next?

indicators.note: the letters have had bad luck and are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A luckless actor boasts in vain that he can foresee the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunate' rearranges ACTOR VAINLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant professes second sight, foreseeing future events.

clue.text: Encouraging shout welcomes one upcoming Greek character, retsina lover?

indicators.note: the shout takes the others inside, welcoming them

parts.note: ole is the Spanish shout of encouragement

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheering crowd welcomes a Greek figure on the way up, fond of retsina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reverses 'one', as the clue reads up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a wine connoisseur; retsina is a Greek wine, so its fan is one example.

clue.text: Old cinema in decline? No, OK with new format

indicators.note: giving the letters a new format rearranges them

explanation.surface: Is the old picture house declining? No, it's doing fine with a new format.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new format' rearranges DECLINE, NO and OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickelodeons were early twentieth-century cinemas charging a nickel for admission.

clue.text: Arrive around gym time and get into contest

indicators.note: the arrive word goes around the others

parts.note: to come is to arrive
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Turn up for gym class on time and enter the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to take part in a contest.

clue.text: Female artist on way back? Very much

indicators.note: going back along the way means the artist's letters run the other way

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A woman painter is heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' turns RA into AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Far is used as an intensifier, as in 'far better', meaning by a great deal.

clue.text: Pattern favouring stubborn person changed in the end

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word is altered to a different one

parts.note: a mule is an obstinate person

explanation.surface: A design backing a pig-headed person is altered at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed in the end' turns MULE into MULA.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a set method or model to follow, a pattern.

clue.text: Mark literary character as potentially most weary

indicators.note: the letters could potentially be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A marker labels a fictional hero as possibly the most worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb but belongs to Mark Twain, whose character this is; 'potentially' rearranges MOST WEARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is the boy hero of Mark Twain's novel, a figure in his fiction.

clue.text: Swiftly take off with Bill aboard

indicators.note: the bill word is carried on board, inside the other

parts.note: to ape is to mimic, to take someone off
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Depart quickly with Bill on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' means impersonate, not depart.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an old adverb meaning quickly.

clue.text: Pressure, impulse, leading to measure to force dissidents out

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: Pressure and impulse together lead a regime to expel its dissidents.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is a political clear-out removing opponents from a party or state.

clue.text: Hostile, rowdy men easily upset nurses

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
to nurse is to hold, so these words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Unruly men who are easily upset nurse grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' points to letters held in rowdY MEN Easily, and 'upset' turns them over to read upwards. 'rowdy' is no anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemy works as an adjective, as in enemy forces, meaning hostile.

clue.text: Brought by visitor, eg a novelty herb

indicators.note: the answer is carried along inside these words, brought by them

explanation.surface: A guest arrives bearing something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought by' points to the letters in visitOR EG A NOvelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic plant of the mint family used in cooking.

clue.text: Henry blocking award for law expert

indicators.note: Henry blocks the award, standing in its middle

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry stands in the way of a legal specialist's honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'law expert' looks like a lawyer; it is Georg Ohm, of Ohm's law.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohm formulated Ohm's law relating voltage, current and resistance.

clue.text: Bitter, furiously, about introduction of usurper's payment

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the single letter, enclosing it
acting furiously throws the letters into disorder
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A bitter subject angrily complains about paying a usurper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furiously' rearranges BITTER into TRIBTE, and 'about' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute was a payment exacted by a ruler or conqueror from subjects.

clue.text: Embarrassing display witnessed, reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is heard, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: witnessed means seen

explanation.surface: Someone's public embarrassment has been observed by others.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a scene is to cause a public fuss or emotional outburst.

clue.text: Soldier happy to accept Church article on return

indicators.note: the happy word takes in the other letters, accepting them

parts.note: merry means happy
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: returning sends the article back so its letters run backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cheerful soldier welcomes back a church item.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary is a hired soldier fighting for pay rather than country.
